summary: Russia launched a large-scale drone and missile attack on August 4-5, targeting Kyiv and other regions with 115 Shahed drones and 24 Iskander-M ballistic missiles, of which Ukrainian air defenses shot down 98. Ukrainian forces struck Russian logistics and military infrastructure including an FSB base in Kherson, bridges in Kursk and Zaporizhzhia, and a drone communication hub in Crimea. The US imposed new sanctions on Russian defense structures while Ukraine faces ongoing economic disruption from port blockades and industrial attacks.
key_points: On the night of August 4-5, Russia launched 115 attack drones (mostly Shahed), 24 Iskander-M ballistic missiles, and 4 anti-ship missiles at Ukraine; Ukrainian forces shot down 98 drones and suppressed others (Source: @kpszsu/71587).

Ukrainian forces struck an FSB base in Kherson, a vehicle bridge over the Seim River in Kursk, a railway bridge over the Molochna River in Zaporizhzhia, and a drone communication/retranslation tower with EW equipment in Crimea (Source: @UkraineNow/83187).

Russia attacked multiple Ukrainian logistics and retail facilities including Novus Ukraine, Brokbridge, Nova Poshta, Rosetka Terminal, Fozzy Group, Silpo Food, Plastmas, Raben Ukraine, Yevrobeton, and Epicenter-K (Source: @eRadarrua/104140).

A fire at a major Wildberries logistics center in Alexin, Tula region of Russia was reported, alongside destruction of Epicenter's ceramic plant in Kiliivtsi with one fatality and three injuries (Source: @UkraineNow/83204, @UkraineNow/83206).

US sanctions targeted Russia's Main Rocket and Artillery Directorate, Ground Forces, and research units, plus entities from Malaysia, Taiwan, Iran, Syria, China, and North Korea (Source: @UkraineNow/83193).

Ukraine's Defense Intelligence claims Russia is preparing a covert mobilization due to declining contract soldier recruitment, with only 200,000 contracts signed in H1 2026 (Source: @UkraineNow/83194).
Ukraine's agricultural exports face up to $3 billion losses this year due to blocked ports in Odessa, Chornomorsk, and Yuzhny since July 22 (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32176).

sections.executive_summary: Russia conducted a major overnight drone and missile barrage on August 4-5, launching 115 Shahed drones, 24 Iskander-M ballistic missiles, and 4 anti-ship missiles targeting Kyiv and other regions. Ukrainian air defenses shot down 98 enemy drones and suppressed additional threats. In retaliation, Ukrainian forces struck Russian logistics hubs, bridges, and military installations across Kherson, Kursk, Zaporizhzhia, and Crimea.

points: On the night of August 4-5, Russia launched a massive attack involving 115 Shahed drones, 24 Iskander-M ballistic missiles, and 4 anti-ship missiles (Tsirkon/Onyx) from Kursk and Rostov regions. Ukrainian air defenses, including aviation, anti-aircraft missile troops, EW units, and mobile fire groups, shot down or suppressed 98 enemy drones (Source: @kpszsu/71587).

Ukrainian forces conducted precision strikes on Russian military infrastructure including an FSB unit deployment point in Kherson Oblast, a vehicle bridge over the Seim River in Kursk Oblast, and a railway bridge over the Molochna River in Zaporizhzhia. Additionally, a drone communication and retransmission tower with EW equipment in Crimea was targeted (Source: @UkraineNow/83187).

Multiple Ukrainian logistics and retail facilities were destroyed by Russian missile and drone attacks, including Novus Ukraine, Brokbridge, Nova Poshta, Rosetka Terminal, Fozzy Group, Silpo Food, Plastmas, Raben Ukraine, Yevrobeton, and Epicenter-K. These attacks caused fires and significant infrastructure damage (Source: @eRadarrua/104140).

A fire broke out at one of the largest Wildberries logistics centers in Alexin, Tula region of Russia. Separately, Russian missiles destroyed Epicenter's ceramic plant in Kiliivtsi, killing one employee and injuring three others. The company announced a two-year recovery timeline and plans to relocate production abroad (Source: @UkraineNow/83204, @UkraineNow/83206).

Ukrainian FPV drones targeted a civilian ATB delivery truck in Kherson's Tavriiskyi district during food delivery, causing the vehicle to catch fire. In Kharkiv, a 'banderole' attack on a civilian enterprise in Novobavarsky district injured eight people (Source: @UkraineNow/83213).

Ukraine's agricultural sector faces up to $3 billion in losses this year due to the ongoing blockade of ports in Odessa, Chornomorsk, and Yuzhny since July 22. No foreign cargo vessels have entered or departed these ports since the blockade began (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/32176).

The Ukrainian government is organizing emergency meetings with business representatives following mass Russian attacks. Economy Minister Kortytsky emphasized that attacks on civilian infrastructure constitute terrorism, not warfare (Source: @UkraineNow/83211).

Russia's air defense forces claimed to have shot down 10 aircraft bombs, 2 HIMARS rockets, and 1,083 Ukrainian drones over the past 24 hours. Russian military reported inflicting approximately 1,380 Ukrainian casualties during the same period (Source: @tass_agency/388822).

Russian forces conducted strikes on Ukrainian energy and transportation infrastructure used by Ukrainian forces. The Russian Ministry of Defense reported successful engagement of these targets but provided no specific location details (Source: @tass_agency/388822).

Russia is reportedly preparing a covert mobilization due to declining contract soldier recruitment. Deputy Security Council Chairman Dmitry Medvedev acknowledged that only 200,000 contracts were signed in H1 2026, representing a 5-11% decrease from the previous year (Source: @UkraineNow/83194).

Putin held a meeting with Russian Ministry of Defense leadership, during which he announced the consolidation of all rear-area services under a single command structure. Valery Solodchuk was appointed to oversee this reorganization (Source: @tass_agency/388812, @tass_agency/388814).

Russian FPV drones were documented hunting civilians in Kherson, with footage showing a drone pursuing an unarmed market vendor in the Tavriiskyi district. The vendor posed no military threat (Source: @UkraineNow/83188).

Russian missile strikes destroyed a major Wildberries logistics center in Alexin, Tula region. The facility was one of the largest in the region, though casualty details were not specified (Source: @UkraineNow/83204).

Russian forces launched coordinated attacks using Iskander-M ballistic missiles from Bryansk and Kursk regions, along with Tsirkon and Onyx anti-ship missiles from naval assets. These formed part of the August 4-5 mass assault (Source: @kpszsu/71587).

Ukrainian forces reported enemy advances near Ustinivka, though specific details about the nature or scale of the movement were not provided. The DeepState map was updated to reflect this development (Source: @DeepStateUA/23719).

Russian forces launched 24 Iskander-M ballistic missiles from Bryansk and Kursk regions as part of the August 4-5 attack wave. These missiles formed a significant component of the coordinated assault on Ukrainian territory (Source: @kpszsu/71587).

Ukrainian Defense Intelligence reported that Russian contract soldier recruitment fell by 5-11% in the first half of 2026 compared to the previous year, with only 200,000 contracts signed. An additional 16,000 joined volunteer formations (Source: @UkraineNow/83194).

Russian forces utilized Iskander-M systems in Bryansk and Kursk regions for their high mobility, launching attacks and quickly relocating to avoid counterstrikes. Ukrainian intelligence noted these systems operate from forested or camouflaged positions (Source: @eRadarrua/104141).

Ukrainian forces struck repair units of the Russian army in Zaporizhzhia and Donetsk regions. Specific details about the targets or damage were not disclosed in the initial reports (Source: @UkraineNow/83187).

Three reactive Shahed drones were detected moving from Bryansk region toward Chernihiv region. The drones were tracked but no engagement details were provided (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69796, @mon1tor_ua/69795).

Ukrainian air defense forces reported a possible ballistic missile threat from the north-east direction. No specific impact locations or interception results were detailed (Source: @eRadarrua/104136).

sections.threat_assessment: The August 4-5 Russian attack represents a significant escalation in the scale and coordination of drone and missile warfare, with 115 Shahed drones and 24 Iskander-M ballistic missiles launched simultaneously from multiple directions. Ukrainian air defenses successfully intercepted 98 enemy drones, demonstrating improved defensive capabilities, but the sheer volume of attacks indicates Russia's intent to overwhelm defenses through saturation. The targeting of civilian infrastructure including logistics centers, retail facilities, and residential areas suggests a deliberate campaign to destabilize Ukraine's economic and social fabric. Russian forces continue to employ high-mobility Iskander-M systems from forested positions, complicating Ukrainian counterstrike efforts. The involvement of North Korean, Iranian, and Chinese entities in Russian defense supply chains, as revealed by US sanctions, indicates expanding international support for Russia's war effort.
sections.regional_response: The United States has responded to Russia's intensified campaign by imposing new sanctions on Russian defense structures and international entities supporting the war effort. These sanctions target the Main Rocket and Artillery Directorate, Ground Forces, and research units, along with companies from Malaysia, Taiwan, Iran, Syria, China, and North Korea. Ukraine's government has organized emergency meetings with business representatives to address the disruption of logistics and commercial operations following mass Russian attacks. The Ukrainian government is working to ensure continuous operation of logistics companies and trade enterprises despite ongoing Russian terror campaigns. Belarusian entrepreneurs have expressed concern over Ukrainian strikes on Wildberries facilities in Russia, requesting government intervention to protect stored goods and sellers.
sections.intelligence_notes: Ukrainian Defense Intelligence reports that Russia is preparing a covert mobilization due to declining contract soldier recruitment, with only 200,000 contracts signed in H1 2026 representing a 5-11% decrease from the previous year. This recruitment shortfall may indicate waning domestic support for the war or logistical challenges in maintaining volunteer forces. The SBU claims to have attacked over 100 rear-line facilities and 21,000 front-line targets during a 40-day operation, though the impact on frontline dynamics remains unspecified. Russian forces continue to utilize high-mobility Iskander-M systems from camouflaged positions, requiring real-time satellite connectivity for effective Ukrainian counterstrikes. The reported request for Starlink access to enable real-time drone operations against mobile Russian missile systems represents a significant intelligence and operational consideration.
